recipes.name: Easy Spanakopita
ingredients_raw: 2 (10 ounce) packages frozen chopped spinach, thawed and well drained
1 (16 ounce) package whole wheat phyllo dough

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Lightly grease a baking sheet. Mix the spinach, feta cheese, mozzarella cheese, Parmesan cheese, garlic, and salt in a bowl.

Arrange one sheet of phyllo dough on a clean work surface and brush with melted butter. Cover the remaining phyllo dough with a damp towel. Place a second sheet of phyllo on top and brush with butter, then place a third sheet on top. Cut the buttered phyllo lengthwise into four strips.

Place about 1 tablespoon of the spinach mixture on the bottom of each strip. Take the bottom right corner and fold the dough over the filling to make a triangle. Fold the bottom left corner up to make another triangle. Continue folding until all the dough is folded. Arrange the stuffed triangles, seam-side down, on the prepared baking sheet. Lightly brush the triangle with butter. Repeat with the remaining phyllo dough and spinach filling.
Bake spanakopita triangles in the preheated oven until golden brown, about 20 minutes. Cool slightly before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Spanakopita
raw_recipe.description: Spanakopita made with phyllo dough, frozen spinach, and 3 types of cheese baked until golden and perfectly crisp for a homemade Greek pastry treat.

review.reviewBody: I am greek and this is the way to make spinach pie. however, sometimes the mix 1-2 eggs with spinach and cheese and it makes a difference. Other times, I saute dried onion and add anise or fennel and I add them to the mixture. Many times i do both,,,, Only reason i dont put 5 stars is because with home made fyllo is superb,,,,

Fantastic recipe! I too added an egg and a few more seasonings. I've done this making the triangles but when in a hurry, rolling the phyllo up strudel style saves time. Bake it whole and slice when slightly cooled. Thank you!

This was very good. I tweaked a bit. I added 2 tbsp of fresh dill and 2 eggs into spinach. Sauté an onion in butter and throw in the spinach mixture as well (it will help dry out as others have said). I omitted the mozzarella. Yiayia would be proud.

Made this last night, did not use the Parmesan or the mozzarella but used more feta, and grated some nutmeg in as well. No need for the salt with the salty feta. I used fresh spinach chopped finely to which I added the egg, minced garlic and onion. Used a couple phyllo sheets laid flat, more filling, folding the sides up and fold like a nice present brushed with butter. Cook on parchment paper, ready in 20 minutes....was AWESOME with a greek salad on the side.
** make sure your phyllo is thawed prior, is already finicky to work with.

This is a delicious recipe as is. It is very simple, and you could even make it simpler by only doing feta cheese. You can't go wrong with spinach, phyllo, feta, and butter. Done deal.

Adding in the parm/mozz adds dimension, which is nice. As other reviewers have said, adding an egg would help with binding and creaminess. You could sautee the garlic before hand with onions before adding to the mixture. Definitely don't skip the step of thoroughly draining your spinach (I like to put in flour sack towel and twist until you can't get any more liquid to come out). It makes a HUGE difference in the end result.

I also don't know how you get by with just 1/2 cup butter. You need to put a lot of butter. I ended up using 2 sticks+ by the end of it, and it made 20 triangles. I also stuffed a bit more spinach mixture in each to make them fatter (2 tbsp instead of 1). The phyllo can handle it if it's well buttered.

But it's delish plain and simple too. You don't always need elaborate recipes, so this one is great as is.

Good recipe, but I have some revisions. I've been making this for years, and I highly recommend using fresh spinach. I also only use feta cheese, about 2 cups. I believe people starting using other cheeses is to keep costs down. The only other things I put into my mix are 2 eggs, which as other users have attested really makes a difference, and a bundle of chopped scallions.

If you are in a hurry, or simply don't feel like making the traditional triangular pieces. you can cook in a 9X13 baking dish. The filo dough should fit without any cutting. Layer the dough, buttering between each. I do 20 layers, then filling, then 20 more, buttering between again. Baking time and temperature remain the same. Hope this helps!

Great recipe! I added two eggs and lots of fresh parsley. I also sautéed the spinach with onions and dried dill in a little olive oil, like Diane Stern mentioned. I cut the phyllo into 3 strips instead of four and added sesame seeds to the top after rolling the pastries. The larger size did require some additional baking time - about 30 minutes at 375 degrees Fahrenheit and then 2-3 minutes of broiling to brown the top at the end. Absolutely amazing!

Excellent. They take about 40 minutes to cook when frozen.

I used fresh mixed greens (chard, kale, spinach) sauteed lightly with onion. I also added more feta and left out the salt as per a previous review.

Wonderful recipe. I have made this several times, the last several changing it a little solely due to my daughter's dietary restrictions. Rather than using butter I substituted olive oil, using a dispenser so I didn't have to use a brush between the layers. I also reduced the amount of cheese a bit and increased the spinach. My entire family LOVED it!! They have asked me to keep making it that way.

Awesome recipe! The mixture for the filling is fantastic! Very tasty and not too salty or greasy. 

I used an easier method (see below) by using full phyllo sheets:

Variation: Butter a 9 by 13 inch baking pan, and spread 6 sheets of filo, brushing each with butter, on the bottom. Spoon the spinach filling over the filo, then cover with 6 more sheets of filo, buttering each sheet. Score the top 3 sheets with a sharp knife. Bake 40 to 45 minutes, or until top is golden, let stand 15 minutes, then cut into squares and serve warm.

I added 2 eggs & put in about 1.5 c feta (no mozz or parm), and threw in some extra seasoning -- a little nutmeg, some dried onion, oregano, etc. And I rolled them up into little "cigars". Very yummy!
Amazing! We decided to add a bit of lemon zest to the filling for a little acid and added in 1/4 cup fresh onion. So easy and fun to make!
This is so good!! I used phyllo cups to make it quicker and they turned out perfect! I didn't have enough mozzarella and used provolone.

This was super easy to follow and very delicious! I was a little confused on the rolling of the dough and I think I bought the wrong amount of dough, but I made it up and still so yummy! This is also easily made low cal/low fat by substituting the cheeses for low fat/cal varieties and the dough is whole wheat!

This is an awesome terrific recipe, and everyone loves me more when I make it. I follow the recipe as closely as possible. The only thing I do differently is cut the phyllo sheets into 3 strips instead of 4 strips, because I like them to be a little larger and easier to grab.
Great recipe. Easy too. I will definitely make again.

It's excellent.

If you find yourself in a time crunch, you can always use cooking spray between phyllo layers instead of melted butter. It's still delicious.

This recipe was delicious and much easier than I expected it to be, even though it does take time to prep and assemble. I combined this recipe with another, but kind of regretted that later because this one was much easier! I added a sauteed onion, a little extra feta cheese and 1/2 cup of parsley, black pepper, and 2 eggs to the spinach/cheese mixture as other reviewers recommended.

I made it exactly the same it wasnt wet enough I think two eggs would have been better. And I didn't wrap it I made it like a pie which I didn't care for. Overall I think it needs wrapped but has a great taste.
